message.content:
I ended my turn without building or trading. I kept the full $456 because my next roll could land me on one of p4's light blues (Oriental, Vermont or Connecticut, 4 houses each), and those rents run $450–500.

If I build on Atlantic ($150) I'd drop to $306. A light-blue hit would then force me to sell houses or mortgage Atlantic. Once I'm past that stretch I'll put the cash into more yellow houses.
message.reasoning:
With $456 at GO, I'm wary of the upcoming light-blue properties with 4 houses charging $450-500 rent, plus Reading Railroad ahead. I want to keep a buffer around $500, so I'm weighing selling houses or mortgaging Atlantic if I get hit, versus spending $150 to build there and dropping to $306.

Opponent p1 only has $18 though, and Boardwalk is coming up for them while the yellows I own are far from where anyone sits, so my liquidation value of $280 from mortgaging Atlantic and selling houses gives me room. I think it's safer to just hold the cash and end my turn.
